title.zh: 卷九十五 列傳第二十 高儉五世孫:重 竇威侄:軌 琮 抗 侄孫:靜 誕 侄:璡 從孫:德玄
title.en: Volume 95 Biographies 20: Gao Jian and Fifth Generation Descendents: Gao Zhong, Dou Weizhi, Douzhi, Dou Gui, Dou Cong, Dou Kang, Dou Jing, Dou Dan, Dou Zhi, Dou Congsun: Dou Dexuan
title.raw: 卷九十五 列傳第二十 高儉五世孫:重 竇威侄:軌 琮 抗 侄孫:靜 誕 侄:璡 從孫:德玄 Volume 95 Biographies 20: Gao Jian and Fifth Generation Descendents: Gao Zhong, Dou Weizhi, Douzhi, Dou Gui, Dou Cong, Dou Kang, Dou Jing, Dou Dan, Dou Zhi, Dou Congsun: Dou Dexuan

sentences.zh: 高檢子:履行 審行 真行 五世孫:重 竇威侄:軌 琮 抗 侄孫:靜 誕 侄:璡 從孫:德玄

translations.literal: Sons of Gao Jian: Lüxing, Shenxing, and Zhenxing; fifth-generation descendant: Zhong; nephews of Dou Wei: Gui, Cong, and Kang; grandnephews: Jing and Dan; nephew: Jin; great-grandnephew: Dexuan.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jian's sons were Lüxing, Shenxing, and Zhenxing; a fifth-generation descendant was Zhong; Dou Wei's nephews were Gui, Cong, and Kang; his grandnephews were Jing and Dan; his nephew was Jin; and his great-grandnephew was Dexuan.

sentences.zh: 高儉，字士廉，以字顯，齊清河王岳之孫，父勵樂安王，入隋為洮州刺史。

translations.literal: Gao Jian, courtesy name Shilian, was known by his courtesy name; he was grandson of Gao Yue, Prince of Qinghe of Northern Qi; his father Li was Prince of Le'an; entering Sui he became governor of Taozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jian, styled Shilian and known by that name, was a grandson of Gao Yue, Prince of Qinghe under the Northern Qi. His father Li held the title Prince of Le'an and, after the dynasty changed, served the Sui as governor of Taozhou.

sentences.zh: 士廉敏惠有度量，狀貌若畫，觀書一見輒誦，敏於占對。

translations.literal: Shilian was clever and generous in spirit; his appearance was as if painted; upon seeing a book once he could recite it; he was quick in impromptu replies.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian was quick-witted and magnanimous, with features so fine they seemed painted. A single reading of a text was enough for him to recite it, and he was equally sharp in conversation.

sentences.zh: 隋司隸大夫薛道衡、起居舍人崔祖浚皆宿臣顯重，與為忘年友，繇是有名。

translations.literal: The Sui officials Xue Daoheng, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Cui Zujun, Attendant Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat, were both veteran ministers of great standing; they became his friends despite the age gap, and thereby he gained renown.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Daoheng, a senior minister of the Sui, and Cui Zujun of the Palace Secretariat were both eminent old servants of the court. They befriended him across the difference in their years, and from that time his name spread.

sentences.zh: 自以齊宗室，不欲廣交，屏居終南山下。

translations.literal: Considering himself a member of the Qi imperial clan, he did not wish to make many acquaintances and withdrew to live at the foot of Mount Zhongnan.
translations.idiomatic: As a scion of the Qi royal house, he avoided wide social ties and lived in seclusion below Mount Zhongnan.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎高孝基勸之仕，仁壽中，舉文才甲科，補治禮郎。

translations.literal: Gao Xiaoji, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, urged him to take office; in the Renshou era he was placed in the top class of the literary talent examination and was appointed Lang of Ritual Regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xiaoji, vice minister of personnel, persuaded him to enter service. During Renshou he passed the literary examination in the highest grade and was appointed an officer of ritual regulation.

sentences.zh: 斛斯政奔高麗，坐與善，貶為硃鳶主簿，以母老不可居瘴癘地，乃留妻鮮于奉養而行。

translations.literal: When Husizheng fled to Goguryeo, he was punished for association with him and demoted to registrar of Zhuyuan; because his mother was old and could not live in a malarial region, he left his wife Xianyu to care for her and went alone.
translations.idiomatic: After Husizheng defected to Goguryeo, Shilian was implicated for their friendship and demoted to registrar at Zhuyuan. His mother was too old to endure the southern marshes, so he left his wife Xianyu to look after her and set out by himself.

sentences.zh: 會世大亂，京師阻絕，交趾太守丘和署司法書佐。

translations.literal: It happened that the realm fell into great disorder and the capital was cut off; Qiu He, governor of Jiaozhi, appointed him judicial secretary.
translations.idiomatic: The empire then plunged into chaos and contact with the capital was lost. Qiu He, governor of Jiaozhi, gave him a post as judicial secretary.

sentences.zh: 時欽州俚帥寧長真以兵侵交趾，和懼，欲出迎，士廉曰：「長真兵雖多，縣軍遠客，勢不得久，城中勝兵尚可戰，奈何受制於人？

translations.literal: At the time the Li chieftain Ning Changzhen of Qinzhou invaded Jiaozhi with troops; Qiu He was afraid and wished to go out to receive him. Shilian said: "Although Changzhen's troops are numerous, as a distant expeditionary force they cannot remain long; the city's able soldiers can still fight—why submit to another's control?
translations.idiomatic: The Li leader Ning Changzhen of Qinzhou was then raiding Jiaozhi with an army. Qiu He grew fearful and meant to go out and surrender. Shilian said, "Changzhen may have many men, but his is a distant campaign and he cannot stay. We still have fit troops in the city—why let ourselves be mastered by him?

sentences.zh: 」和因命為行軍司馬，逆擊破之。

translations.literal: " Qiu He thereupon appointed him campaigning marshal and, attacking in counterstroke, defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: " Qiu He then named him campaigning marshal, and Shilian met the invaders head-on and routed them.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣使徇嶺南，武德五年與和來降，於是秦王領雍州牧，薦士廉為治中，親重之。

translations.literal: Gaozu sent envoys to pacify Lingnan; in the fifth year of Wude he and Qiu He came to surrender. Thereupon the Prince of Qin, holding the post of governor of Yongzhou, recommended Shilian as administrative aide and treated him with personal regard.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu sent agents to bring the south under control, Shilian and Qiu He submitted in the fifth year of Wude. The Prince of Qin, now governor of Yongzhou, recommended him as administrative aide and held him in close esteem.

sentences.zh: 隱太子與王隙已熾，乃與長孫無忌密計計定，是日率吏卒釋囚授甲，趨芳林門助戰。

translations.literal: The rift between the Hidden Crown Prince and the Prince of Qin had already grown fierce; he then secretly laid plans with Zhangsun Wuji, and on that day led clerks and soldiers to release prisoners, arm them, and hurry to Fanglin Gate to aid in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: By then the breach between the Hidden Crown Prince and the Prince of Qin had turned bitter. Shilian worked out a secret plan with Zhangsun Wuji, and that day led clerks and troops to free prisoners, put arms on them, and rush to Fanglin Gate to join the battle.

sentences.zh: 王為皇太子，授右庶子。

translations.literal: When the Prince became crown prince, he was appointed Right Vice Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: After the prince was made heir apparent, Shilian was appointed right vice mentor of the heir.

sentences.zh: 進侍中，封義興郡公。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Duke of Yixing commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace attendant and created Duke of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 坐匿王珪奏不時上，左授安州都督。

translations.literal: For concealing Wang Gui's memorial and not forwarding it in time, he was demoted to military commissioner of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished for withholding Wang Gui's memorial and failing to submit it promptly, and was demoted to military commissioner of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 進益州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: He was advanced to chief administrator of the Yizhou Grand Protectorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to chief administrator of the Yizhou metropolitan command.

sentences.zh: 蜀人畏鬼而惡疾，雖父母病皆委去，望舍投餌哺之，昆弟不相假財。

translations.literal: The people of Shu feared ghosts and loathed illness; even when parents were sick they abandoned them, casting food from afar toward the house to feed them, and brothers would not lend one another money.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu feared spirits and shunned the sick. Even parents were abandoned in illness; kin would toss food toward the dwelling from a distance rather than enter, and brothers would not lend one another money.

sentences.zh: 士廉為設條教，辯告督勵，風俗翕然為變。

translations.literal: Shilian established regulations, explained and exhorted them, and supervised encouragement until custom swiftly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian drew up regulations, explained them plainly, and pressed for compliance until local custom changed almost at once.

sentences.zh: 又引諸生講授經藝，學校復興。

translations.literal: He also brought in students to lecture on the classics, and schools flourished again.
translations.idiomatic: He also gathered students to teach the classics, and the schools revived.

sentences.zh: 秦時李冰導汶江水灌田，瀕水者頃千金，民相侵冒。

translations.literal: In Qin times Li Bing diverted the Min River to irrigate fields; land along the water was worth a thousand gold per mou, and the people encroached on one another.
translations.idiomatic: Since Qin times Li Bing had channeled the Min to irrigate the fields. Land along the water was worth a fortune, and neighbors constantly encroached on one another.

sentences.zh: 士廉附故渠廝引旁出，以廣溉道，人以富饒。

translations.literal: Shilian attached to the old canal and drew branches outward to broaden the irrigation channels, and the people became wealthy.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian extended the old canal with side channels to widen irrigation, and the people grew prosperous.

sentences.zh: 入為吏部尚書，進封許國公。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of the State of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as minister of personnel and was advanced to Duke of Xu.

sentences.zh: 雅負裁鑒，又詳氏譜，所署州，人地無不當者。

translations.literal: He was famed for judgment in appointments and was also expert in clan genealogies; in every prefecture he assigned, men and posts were never ill matched.
translations.idiomatic: He was renowned for discerning appointments and knew genealogies thoroughly. In every post he filled, the man and the place always suited each other.

sentences.zh: 高祖崩，攝司空，營山陵；

translations.literal: When Gaozu died, he acted as Minister of Works and oversaw the imperial tomb;
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu's death he served as acting minister of works and directed construction of the imperial tomb;

sentences.zh: 加特進，遷尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: he was given the special advancement rank and transferred to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: he received the rank of special advancement and was moved to right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 士廉三世居此官，世榮其貴。

translations.literal: Shilian's family for three generations held this office, and the age honored their eminence.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations of his line had held that office, and their contemporaries took pride in the family's standing.

sentences.zh: 太宗幸洛陽，太子監國，命攝少師。

translations.literal: When Taizong visited Luoyang and the crown prince supervised the state, he was ordered to act as Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong went to Luoyang and the crown prince remained to govern, Shilian was appointed acting junior tutor.

sentences.zh: 手詔曰：「端拱三川，不憂關中者，以屬卿也。

translations.literal: An imperial letter in the emperor's own hand said: "Sitting at ease in the Three Rivers region, I do not worry about Guanzhong because I entrust it to you.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote in his own hand, "I can rest easy in the Three Rivers and not fret over Guanzhong because I leave it in your charge.

sentences.zh: 」久之，請致仕，聽解僕射，加開府儀同三司、同中書門下三品，知政事。

translations.literal: " After a long while he requested retirement; he was permitted to resign the vice directorship, was given Grand Master with Golden Casque and Three Honors with the same Three-Grade rank as the Secretariat-Chancellery, and took part in governance.
translations.idiomatic: " In time he asked to retire. He was allowed to step down as vice director, was given the honors of grand master with golden casque and three parallels, was made third-grade colleague of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and continued to handle state affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝伐高麗，皇太子監國駐定州，又攝太傅，同掌機務。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned against Goguryeo, the crown prince supervised the state from Dingzhou; he again acted as Grand Tutor and jointly managed critical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Goguryeo the crown prince governed from Dingzhou. Shilian again served as acting grand tutor and shared control of urgent business.

sentences.zh: 太子令曰：「寡人資公訓道，而比聽政，據桉對公，情所未安，所司宜別設桉奉太傅。

translations.literal: The crown prince ordered: "I rely on you, sir, for instruction, yet in recent audiences I sit at the desk facing you, which my heart cannot rest with; the offices should set up a separate desk for the Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince ordered, "I depend on you for guidance, yet in court I sit at the same desk facing you, which I find awkward. The offices should provide a separate desk for the grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 」士廉固辭。

translations.literal: " Shilian firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: " Shilian firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 士廉進止詳華，凡有獻納，搢紳皆屬以目。

translations.literal: Shilian's deportment in court was measured and splendid; whenever he offered counsel, the gentry all fixed their eyes on him.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian's bearing at court was dignified and precise. Whenever he offered advice, the officials all watched him closely.

sentences.zh: 奏議未嘗不焚稿，家人無見者。

translations.literal: He never failed to burn his memorial drafts; none in his household ever saw them.
translations.idiomatic: He always burned his draft memorials afterward, and no one in his household ever saw them.

sentences.zh: 士廉少識太宗非常人，以所出女歸之，是為文德皇后。

translations.literal: Shilian early recognized that Taizong was no ordinary man and gave him a daughter by his wife; she became Empress Wende.
translations.idiomatic: While still young Shilian saw that Taizong was no ordinary man and gave him his daughter in marriage. She became Empress Wende.

sentences.zh: 及遺令墓不得它藏，惟置衣一襲與平生所好書示先王典訓可用終始者。

translations.literal: In his final instructions he ordered that the tomb hold no other possessions, only one suit of clothes and the books he had loved in life showing the former kings' canonical teachings usable from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: His last instructions allowed nothing else in the tomb but one suit of clothes and the books he had cherished—those classical teachings of the former kings that could guide a life from start to finish.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗嘗以山東士人尚閥閱，後雖衰，子孫猶負世望，嫁娶必多取貲，故人謂之賣昏。

translations.literal: Earlier Taizong had remarked that the gentry east of the mountains prized pedigree; though later in decline, their descendants still bore the prestige of old families, and in marriage they always demanded much wealth—hence people called it selling a marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong had once observed that the eastern gentry still prized pedigree. Even when their houses declined, descendants traded on old renown and demanded heavy bride-prices at marriage, so people spoke of "selling a wedding."

sentences.zh: 由是詔士廉與韋挺、岑文本、令狐德棻責天下譜諜，參考史傳，檢正真偽，進忠賢，退悖惡，先宗室，後外戚，退新門，進舊望，右膏粱，左寒畯，合二百九十三姓，千六百五十一家，為九等，號曰《氏族志》，而崔幹仍居第一。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Shilian, together with Wei Ting, Cen Wenben, and Linghu Defen, to take charge of genealogies throughout the realm, consult historical records, verify truth and falsehood, advance the loyal and worthy and remove the perverse and wicked, put the imperial clan first and consort kin after, demote new houses and advance old standing, favor the well-born on the right and the humble scholar on the left—altogether two hundred ninety-three surnames and one thousand six hundred fifty-one families in nine grades, titled the Record of Clans; yet Cui Gan still ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore charged Shilian, Wei Ting, Cen Wenben, and Linghu Defen to compile genealogies empire-wide, check them against the histories, advance the worthy and exclude the corrupt, rank the imperial clan before affinal kin, favor old houses over parvenus, and place eminent birth to the right and poor scholars to the left. They listed 293 surnames in 1,651 families in nine grades as the Record of Clans, yet Cui Gan still stood first.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「我于崔、盧、李、鄭無嫌，顧其世衰，不復冠冕，猶恃舊地以取貲，不肖子偃然自高，販鬻松檟，不解人間何為貴之？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I bear no grudge against the Cui, Lu, Li, and Zheng clans, but their age has declined and they no longer fill high offices; they still rely on old standing to extract wealth, and unworthy sons hold themselves loftily, peddling their pedigree like selling coffin wood—I do not understand why the world still esteems them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have no quarrel with the Cui, Lu, Li, and Zheng lines, but their day is past. They no longer hold high office yet still trade on old names for money. Worthless sons strut as if noble, hawking their ancestry like coffin timber. I cannot see why anyone still honors them.

sentences.zh: 齊據河北，梁、陳在江南，雖有人物，偏方下國，無可貴者，故以崔、盧、王、謝為重。

translations.literal: Qi held Hebei, Liang and Chen were in Jiangnan—though they had men of talent, as marginal lesser states they were not to be prized; therefore the Cui, Lu, Wang, and Xie were held in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Qi held the north, Liang and Chen the south. Talented men they had, but as petty border kingdoms they deserved no special honor—hence the Cui, Lu, Wang, and Xie were exalted instead.

sentences.zh: 今謀士勞臣以忠孝學藝從我定天下者，何容納貨舊門，向聲背實，買昏為榮耶？

translations.literal: Now the strategists and toiling ministers who followed me in establishing the realm through loyalty, filial piety, learning, and arts—how can they admit the old houses for a price, heed reputation against reality, and take buying a marriage as glory?
translations.idiomatic: The counselors and veterans who followed me through loyalty, learning, and service in pacifying the realm—how can they pay old clans for a name, chase reputation over merit, and treat a bought marriage as honor?

sentences.zh: 太上有立德，其次有立功，其次有立言，其次有爵為公、卿、大夫，世世不絕，此謂之門戶。

translations.literal: The highest is establishing virtue, next establishing merit, next establishing words, next holding noble ranks as duke, minister, or grandee generation after generation without end—this is called a house.
translations.idiomatic: First comes establishing virtue, then merit, then lasting words, then hereditary ranks as duke, minister, or grandee passed down without break—that is what makes a true house.

sentences.zh: 今皆反是，豈不惑邪？

translations.literal: Now all is the reverse—is this not delusion?
translations.idiomatic: Now everything is reversed—is that not folly?

sentences.zh: 朕以今日冠冕為等級高下。

translations.literal: I take today's caps and sashes as the measure of rank high and low.
translations.idiomatic: I will rank families by the offices they hold today.

sentences.zh: 」遂以崔幹為第三姓，班其書天下。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Cui Gan was placed as the third surname, and the book was promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ranked the Cui of Gan third and had the register published empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，許敬宗以不敘武后世，又李義府恥其家無名，更以孔志約、楊仁卿、史玄道、呂才等十二人刊定之，裁廣類例，合二百三十五姓，二千二百八十七家，帝自敘所以然。

translations.literal: Under Gaozong, Xu Jingzong, because the Wu empress's line was not recorded, and Li Yifu ashamed that his house was unnamed, again had Kong Zhiyue, Yang Renqing, Shi Xuandao, Lü Cai, and twelve others revise it, trimming and broadening categories—altogether two hundred thirty-five surnames and two thousand two hundred eighty-seven families; the emperor himself explained the reasons.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong, Xu Jingzong omitted Empress Wu's house and Li Yifu, shamed that his clan lacked standing, had Kong Zhiyue, Yang Renqing, Shi Xuandao, Lü Cai, and nine others revise the work. They tightened and expanded the categories to 235 surnames in 2,287 families, and the emperor himself set out his reasons.

sentences.zh: 以四後姓、酅公、介公及三公、太子三師、開府儀同三司、尚書僕射為第一姓，文武二品及知政事三品為第二姓，各以品位高下敘之，凡九等，取身及昆弟子孫，余屬不入，改為《姓氏錄》。

translations.literal: The four empress surnames, the Duke of Xi, the Duke of Jie, and the Three Dukes, the crown prince's three tutors, grand masters with golden casque, and vice directors of the Department of State Affairs were made the first surname; civil and military officials of the second rank and third-rank participants in governance were the second surname; each was ordered by office rank high and low in nine grades, taking only the person and brothers, sons, and grandsons—other kin were excluded—and the title was changed to the Record of Surnames.
translations.idiomatic: The four empress clans, the dukes of Xi and Jie, the three dukes, the crown prince's tutors, grand masters with golden casque, and vice directors formed the first rank; second-rank civil and military officials and third-rank councilors formed the second. All were ordered by current office in nine grades, listing only the man, his brothers, sons, and grandsons. Other kin were dropped, and the work was retitled the Record of Surnames.

sentences.zh: 當時軍功入五品者，皆升譜限，搢紳恥焉，目為「勳格」。

translations.literal: At the time all who entered the fifth rank by military merit were raised within genealogical limits; the gentry were ashamed of this and called it the "merit register."
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who reached fifth rank through military service was elevated in the genealogy, to the gentry's shame—they called it the "merit register."

sentences.zh: 義府奏悉索《氏族志》燒之。

translations.literal: Yifu memorialized to have every copy of the Record of Clans sought out and burned.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu petitioned to have every copy of the Record of Clans collected and burned.

sentences.zh: 又詔後魏隴西李寶，太原王瓊，滎陽鄭溫，范陽盧子遷、盧澤、盧輔，清河崔宗伯、崔元孫，前燕博陵崔懿，晉趙郡李楷，凡七姓十家，不得自為昏；

translations.literal: It was further decreed that the ten houses of seven surnames—Li Bao of Longxi in Later Wei, Wang Qiong of Taiyuan, Zheng Wen of Xingyang, Lu Ziqian, Lu Ze, and Lu Fu of Fanyang, Cui Zongbo and Cui Yuansun of Qinghe, Cui Yi of Boling in Former Yan, and Li Kai of Zhao in Jin—might not intermarry among themselves;
translations.idiomatic: An edict also barred intermarriage among the seven great surnames in ten houses: the Li of Longxi, Wang of Taiyuan, Zheng of Xingyang, three lines of Lu from Fanyang, two lines of Cui from Qinghe, Cui of Boling, and Li of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 三品以上納幣不得過三百匹，四品五品二百，六品七品百，悉為歸裝，夫氏禁受陪門財。

translations.literal: betrothal gifts for third rank and above might not exceed three hundred bolts, for fourth and fifth ranks two hundred, for sixth and seventh ranks one hundred—all to be the bride's trousseau; the husband's clan was forbidden to accept door-companion wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Bride-price for third rank and above was capped at three hundred bolts of silk, two hundred for fourth and fifth ranks, one hundred for sixth and seventh—all counted as the bride's dowry. The groom's family was forbidden to accept supplementary marriage payments.

sentences.zh: 先是，後魏太和中，定四海望族，以寶等為冠。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Taihe era of Later Wei, eminent clans of the four seas were fixed, with Bao and the others at the head.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in Northern Wei's Taihe reign, the leading clans of the realm were defined, with Bao's house foremost among them.

sentences.zh: 其後矜尚門地，故《氏族志》一切降之。

translations.literal: Afterward pedigree was prized, so in the Record of Clans they were all demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when pedigree was again exalted, the Record of Clans demoted them all.

sentences.zh: 王妃、主婿皆取當世勳貴名臣家，未嘗尚山東舊族。

translations.literal: Imperial princesses' husbands and princesses' consorts were all taken from contemporary meritorious and eminent ministerial houses; they never favored the old clans east of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial sons-in-law were chosen from the great ministers and heroes of the day, never from the old eastern aristocracy.

sentences.zh: 後房玄齡、魏徵、李勣復與昏，故望不減，然每姓第其房望，雖一姓中，高下縣隔。

translations.literal: Later Fang Xuanling, Wei Zheng, and Li Ji again intermarried with them, so their prestige did not decline; yet within each surname branches were ranked by standing, and even within one surname high and low were vastly separated.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang Xuanling, Wei Zheng, and Li Ji married into them, their prestige held. Yet each surname ranked its branches, and even within a single name high and low lines stood far apart.

sentences.zh: 李義府為子求昏不得，始奏禁焉。

translations.literal: Li Yifu could not obtain a marriage for his son and thereupon memorialized for the prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yifu failed to secure a match for his son and only then petitioned for the ban.

sentences.zh: 其後天下衰宗落譜，昭穆所不齒者，皆稱「禁昏家」，益自貴，凡男女皆潛相聘娶，天子不能禁，世以為敝雲。

translations.literal: Afterward declining clans dropped from registers, those whom proper lineage would not acknowledge all called themselves "forbidden-marriage houses," prized themselves all the more, and men and women secretly betrothed one another; the Son of Heaven could not forbid it—the age regarded it as a abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Declining lines struck from the registers took the title "forbidden-marriage houses" and grew prouder still. Men and women wed in secret, and even the throne could not stop it—a custom the age judged a corruption.

sentences.zh: 士廉六子，履行、審行、真行有名。

translations.literal: Shilian had six sons; Lüxing, Shenxing, and Zhenxing were renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian had six sons; Lüxing, Shenxing, and Zhenxing were the ones of note.

sentences.zh: 子 履行

translations.literal: Son: Lüxing
translations.idiomatic: His son Lüxing

sentences.zh: 履行居母喪毀甚，太宗諭使強食。

translations.literal: Lüxing in mourning for his mother was so devastated that Taizong admonished him to force himself to eat.
translations.idiomatic: During his mother's mourning Lüxing grieved so severely that Taizong urged him to eat.

sentences.zh: 尚東陽公主，襲爵。

translations.literal: He married Princess Dongyang and inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: He married Princess Dongyang and succeeded to his father's title.

sentences.zh: 繇戶部尚書為益州大都督府長史，政有名。

translations.literal: From Minister of Revenue he became chief administrator of the Yizhou Grand Protectorate, and his governance won renown.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as minister of revenue he became chief administrator of Yizhou, where his rule won praise.

sentences.zh: 坐長孫無忌，左授洪州都督，改永州刺史。

translations.literal: Implicated through Zhangsun Wuji, he was demoted to military commissioner of Hongzhou and then made prefect of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Caught up in Zhangsun Wuji's fall, he was demoted to commissioner of Hongzhou and later transferred to prefect of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 子 真行

translations.literal: Son: Zhenxing
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhenxing

sentences.zh: 真行至左衛將軍。

translations.literal: Zhenxing rose to General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenxing rose to general of the left guard.

sentences.zh: 其子岐連章懷太子事，詔令自誡切，真行以佩刀刺殺之，斷首棄道上，高宗鄙其為，貶睦州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Qi was implicated in the Crown Prince Zhanghuai affair; an edict ordered stern self-reproach, but Zhenxing stabbed him to death with his girdle knife, severed the head, and cast it on the road. Gaozong despised the act and demoted him to prefect of Muzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qi was tied to Crown Prince Zhanghuai's case and ordered to repent sharply. Zhenxing killed him with his own blade, cut off the head, and left it in the street. Gaozong held the act in contempt and demoted him to prefect of Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 子 審行

translations.literal: Son: Shenxing
translations.idiomatic: His son Shenxing

sentences.zh: 審行自戶部侍郎貶渝州刺史。

translations.literal: Shenxing was demoted from Vice Minister of Revenue to prefect of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxing fell from vice minister of revenue to prefect of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 五世孫 重

translations.literal: Fifth-generation descendant: Zhong
translations.idiomatic: Fifth-generation descendant Zhong

sentences.zh: 士廉五世孫重，字文明，以明經中第，李巽表鹽鐵轉運巡官，善職，凡十年，進累司門郎中。

translations.literal: Shilian's fifth-generation descendant Zhong, courtesy name Wenming, passed the classics examination; Li Xun recommended him as salt and iron transport inspector, he performed well for ten years in all, and was advanced through accumulation to Director of the Gate Office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong, Shilian's fifth-generation descendant, styled Wenming, passed the classics examination. Li Xun recommended him as salt-and-iron transport inspector; he served ably for ten years and rose to director of the gate office.

sentences.zh: 敬宗慎置侍講學士，重以簡厚惇正，與崔郾偕選，再擢國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Jingzong carefully appointed lecturing scholars; Zhong, for his simplicity, depth, and integrity, was chosen together with Cui Yan and twice promoted to Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong carefully chose lecturing scholars. Zhong's plain, steadfast character won him selection with Cui Yan, and he was twice promoted to chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 文宗好《左氏春秋》，命分列國各為書，成四十篇。

translations.literal: Wenzong loved the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals and ordered the states each made into separate books, completing forty chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong favored the Zuo Commentary and ordered each state treated as its own book, producing forty chapters.

sentences.zh: 與鄭覃刊定《九經》于石。

translations.literal: Together with Zheng Tan he collated and cut the Nine Classics in stone.
translations.idiomatic: With Zheng Tan he edited the Nine Classics and had them carved on stone.

sentences.zh: 出為鄂嶽觀察使，以美政被褒。

translations.literal: He went out as military commissioner of E-Yue and was praised for excellent governance.
translations.idiomatic: He served as commissioner of E-Yue and was commended for good government.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜太子賓客，分司東都。

translations.literal: After a long while he was appointed Guest of the Heir Apparent with detached service at the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was made guest of the heir apparent with detached duty at the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made junior mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：古者受姓受氏以旌有功，是時人皆土著，故名宗望姓，舉郡國自表，而譜系興焉，所以推敘昭穆，使百代不得相亂也。

translations.literal: The encomium says: In antiquity one received surname and clan name to honor merit; at that time all were native to the soil, hence clans were named by ancestral seat and surname, each commandery and state setting itself forth—and genealogies arose to arrange senior and junior lines so that a hundred generations would not be confused.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: In antiquity surnames and clan names honored merit. People were rooted to their land, so clans took their names from ancestral seats and each region recorded itself—thus genealogies arose to order the generations and keep lineages distinct across the ages.

sentences.zh: 遭晉播遷，胡醜亂華，百宗蕩析，士去墳墓，子孫猶挾系錄，以示所承，而閥閥顯者，至賣昏求財，汨喪廉恥。

translations.literal: When Jin was driven abroad and barbarian hosts troubled China, a hundred clans were scattered; scholars left their tombs, yet descendants still carried registers to show what they inherited—while eminent pedigrees came even to selling marriages for wealth, drowning integrity and shame.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin exile and the barbarian turmoil, clans were shattered and scholars fled their graves, yet descendants still clung to registers to prove descent. Great houses sold marriages for profit and drowned honor in greed.

sentences.zh: 唐初流弊仍甚，天子屢抑不為衰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tang the abuses remained severe; the Son of Heaven repeatedly suppressed them, yet they did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tang abuses persisted, and though emperors repeatedly tried to curb them, pedigree pride did not fade.

sentences.zh: 至中葉，風教又薄，譜錄都廢，公靡常產之拘，士亡舊德之傳，言李悉出隴西，言劉悉出彭城，悠悠世詐，訖無考按，冠冕皁隸，混為一區，可太息哉！

translations.literal: By the mid-dynasty custom had thinned again, genealogies were wholly abandoned, dukes were free of fixed-property constraints, scholars lost transmission of old virtue—every Li was said to come from Longxi, every Liu from Pengcheng; fraud spread through the age with no verification, caps and sashes and common clerks mixed in one mass—how deeply to be sighed over!
translations.idiomatic: By mid-Tang morals had thinned again and genealogies fell into disuse. Great families no longer held to fixed estates, scholars no longer passed down old virtue—every Li was called Longxi, every Liu Pengcheng. Deceit ran on unchecked until lord and clerk were indistinguishable. One can only sigh.

sentences.zh: 竇威，字文蔚，岐州平陸人。

translations.literal: Dou Wei, courtesy name Wenwei, was a man of Pinglu in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wei, styled Wenwei, was from Pinglu in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 父熾，在周為上柱國，入隋為太傅，太穆皇后，其從兄弟女也。

translations.literal: His father Chi was a pillar of state in Zhou; entering Sui he became Grand Tutor. Empress Taimu was a daughter of his paternal cousin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chi was a pillar of state under Zhou and grand tutor under Sui. Empress Taimu was his cousin's daughter.

sentences.zh: 威沈邃有器局，貫覽群言，家世貴，子弟皆喜武力，獨威尚文，諸兄詆為書癡。

translations.literal: Wei was deep and far-reaching in capacity, thoroughly reading all writings; the family was noble for generations, and the sons and younger kin all loved martial prowess—only Wei honored letters, and his elder brothers mocked him as a book fool.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was grave and broad-minded, versed in the classics. His house was eminent, and the younger men favored arms—only Wei loved learning, and his brothers called him a bookish fool.

sentences.zh: 內史令李德林舉秀異，授秘書郎，當遷不肯調者十年，故其學益博。

translations.literal: Li Delin, Director of the Palace Secretariat, recommended him as outstanding talent and appointed him Secretary; when due for transfer he refused reassignment for ten years, and thus his learning grew ever broader.
translations.idiomatic: Li Delin of the Secretariat recommended him as outstanding talent and made him a secretary. For ten years he refused promotion, and his learning grew all the deeper.

sentences.zh: 而諸兄以軍功位通顯矣，薄威職閑冗，更謂曰：「昔仲尼積學成聖，猶棲遲不偶，汝尚何求耶？

translations.literal: Yet his elder brothers had reached high rank through military merit and looked down on Wei's post as idle and trivial, saying again: "In old times Confucius amassed learning and became a sage, yet still lingered without success—what more do you seek?
translations.idiomatic: His brothers had risen by military merit and scorned Wei's quiet post. They said, "Confucius piled up learning until he became a sage, yet still waited long without preferment—what are you still chasing?

sentences.zh: 」威笑不答。

translations.literal: " Wei smiled and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Wei only smiled and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 蜀王秀辟為記室，威以秀多不法，謝疾去。

translations.literal: Prince Xiu of Shu recruited him as secretary; Wei, because Xiu committed many unlawful acts, pleaded illness and left.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiu of Shu made him secretary, but Wei quit on grounds of illness when he saw how lawless the prince was.

sentences.zh: 秀廢，府屬皆得罪，威獨免。

translations.literal: When Xiu was deposed, all staff of the princely establishment were punished; Wei alone was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu was deposed, every member of his staff was punished except Wei.

sentences.zh: 大業中，累遷內史舍人，數諫忤旨，轉考功郎中，後坐事免。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he was repeatedly promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat; he remonstrated many times against the emperor's will, was transferred to Director of the Bureau of Merit, and later was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: During Daye he rose to secretariat attendant but offended the throne with repeated remonstrance, was moved to the merit bureau, and later dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 後寢疾，帝臨問，及卒，哭之慟。

translations.literal: Later he took to his bed in illness; the emperor visited him in inquiry, and when he died the emperor wept for him in deep grief.
translations.idiomatic: He later fell ill; the emperor visited his bedside, and when he died wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 贈同州刺史，追封延安郡公，諡曰靖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the post of prefect of Tongzhou, enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Yan'an commandery, with posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made prefect of Tongzhou and Duke of Yan'an, with the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 威性儉素，家不樹產，比喪，無餘貲，遺令薄葬。

translations.literal: Wei was frugal and plain by nature; the household amassed no property; by the time of his death there was no surplus wealth, and his final instructions ordered a simple burial.
translations.idiomatic: Wei lived simply and left no estate. At his death there was nothing left over, and he ordered a plain burial.

sentences.zh: 詔皇太子、百官臨送。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the crown prince and all officials to attend the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince and the officials were ordered to attend his funeral.

sentences.zh: 侄 軌

translations.literal: Nephew: Gui
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Gui

sentences.zh: 兄子軌，字士則。

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Gui, courtesy name Shize.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's nephew Gui, styled Shize.

sentences.zh: 父恭，仕周為雍州牧、酂國公。

translations.literal: His father Gong served Zhou as governor of Yongzhou and Duke of the State of Zan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gong served Zhou as governor of Yongzhou and Duke of Zan.

sentences.zh: 軌性剛果有威，大業中，為資陽郡東曹掾，去官歸。

translations.literal: Gui was firm, resolute, and commanding; in the Daye era he was eastern bureau clerk of Ziyang commandery, then left office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was stern and forceful. During Daye he served as eastern bureau clerk of Ziyang, then resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 高祖起兵，軌募眾千餘人迎謁長春宮。

translations.literal: When Gaozu raised troops, Gui recruited more than a thousand men and went to pay respects at Changchun Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu rose in arms, Gui raised more than a thousand men and went to Changchun Palace to join him.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，賜良馬十匹，使略地渭南，下永豐倉，收兵五千，從平京師。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, gave him ten fine horses, and sent him to seize territory in Weinan, take Yongfeng granary, gather five thousand troops, and follow in pacifying the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, gave him ten fine horses, and sent him to secure Weinan, capture Yongfeng granary, raise five thousand men, and help take the capital.

sentences.zh: 封贊皇縣公，為大丞相諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Zanhuang county and made consulting aide to the Grand Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He was created Duke of Zanhuang and made consulting aide to the grand chancellor.

sentences.zh: 稽胡賊五萬掠宜春，詔軌討之。

translations.literal: Ji Hu rebels, fifty thousand strong, plundered Yichun; an edict ordered Gui to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty thousand Ji Hu bandits raided Yichun, and the court ordered Dou Gui to go after them.

sentences.zh: 次黃欽山，遇賊乘高叢射，眾為卻。

translations.literal: Halting at Huangqin Mountain, they met rebels shooting down in dense volleys from high ground, and the army fell back.
translations.idiomatic: At Huangqin Mountain the rebels held the heights and rained arrows down on them, forcing the troops to retreat.

sentences.zh: 軌斬部將十四人，更拔其次代之，身擁數百騎殿，令曰：「聞鼓不進者斬。

translations.literal: Gui executed fourteen subordinate officers, promoted their seconds to replace them, personally led several hundred cavalry in the rear, and ordered: 'Whoever hears the drum and does not advance shall be executed.'
translations.idiomatic: Gui beheaded fourteen of his officers on the spot, replaced them with their deputies, took personal command of a few hundred horsemen in the rear, and declared: 'Anyone who fails to advance at the drumbeat will die.'

sentences.zh: 」既鼓，士爭赴賊，賊射不勝，大破之，斬首千級，獲男女二萬。

translations.literal: When the drum sounded, the soldiers rushed to compete with the rebels; the rebels' arrows could not prevail; he routed them utterly, beheading a thousand and capturing twenty thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: At the beat of the drum the men surged forward; the rebels could not shoot them down fast enough. Gui smashed their force, took a thousand heads, and captured twenty thousand people.

sentences.zh: 擢太子詹事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand Steward of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Steward of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 赤排羌與薛舉叛將鐘俱仇寇漢中，拜秦州總管，討賊連戰有功，餘黨悉降。

translations.literal: The Chipa Qiang and Zhong Juqiu, a rebel general of Xue Ju, raided Hanzhong; he was appointed General-in-Chief of Qin Prefecture, fought the rebels in successive battles with merit, and the remnant factions all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chipa Qiang joined Xue Ju's turncoat general Zhong Juqiu in raiding Hanzhong, Gui was made military governor of Qinzhou. He fought them battle after battle with success until every remaining band surrendered.

sentences.zh: 復酂國舊封，遷益州道行台左僕射。

translations.literal: His old fief of Zan State was restored, and he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Yizhou Circuit Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestral fief of Zan was restored, and he was moved to left vice director of the Yizhou circuit headquarters.

sentences.zh: 党項引吐谷渾寇松州，詔軌與扶州刺史蔣善合援之。

translations.literal: The Tangut led the Tuyuhun to raid Song Prefecture; an edict ordered Gui and Fu Prefecture Governor Jiang Shanhe to reinforce it.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut brought the Tuyuhun against Songzhou, and the court ordered Gui and Jiang Shanhe, governor of Fuzhou, to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 善合先期至，敗之鉗川。

translations.literal: Shanhe arrived ahead of time and defeated them at Qianchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shanhe got there first and routed the enemy at Qianchuan.

sentences.zh: 軌進軍臨洮，擊左封，走其眾。

translations.literal: Gui advanced to Lintao, attacked Zuofeng, and put their force to flight.
translations.idiomatic: Gui pushed on to Lintao, struck Zuofeng, and drove the enemy off.

sentences.zh: 度羌必為患，始屯田松州。

translations.literal: Judging that the Qiang would surely become a threat, he began agricultural colonies at Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Convinced the Qiang would only grow more dangerous, he started garrison farming around Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔率所部兵從秦王討王世充。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to lead his troops under the Prince of Qin to campaign against Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him to take his command and join the Prince of Qin in the war against Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 明年，還蜀。

translations.literal: The next year, he returned to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he went back to Shu.

sentences.zh: 軌既貴，益嚴酷，然能自勤苦，每出師臨敵，身未嘗解甲，其下有不用命即誅，至小過亦鞭棰流血，人見者皆重足股忄栗，由是蜀盜悉平。

translations.literal: Once Gui had risen high, he grew still harsher, yet he kept himself to hardship; whenever he marched out to face the enemy he never once removed his armor; subordinates who disobeyed were executed at once, and even minor faults were punished with the whip until blood ran; all who saw it stood on tiptoe in dread, and by this means every bandit in Shu was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Power only made Gui crueler, though he never spared himself: on campaign he slept in his armor, killed men on the spot for insubordination, and flogged even petty offenders until they bled. Everyone who served under him lived in terror, and in time the brigands of Shu were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 初，以其甥為腹心，嘗夜出，呼不時至，斬之。

translations.literal: At first he made his nephew his trusted confidant; once, going out at night, he summoned him and the man did not arrive promptly, so he executed him.
translations.idiomatic: He had once put a nephew at the center of his inner circle; one night he called for the man and, when he failed to come quickly enough, cut off his head.

sentences.zh: 又戒家奴毋出外，忽遣奴取漿公廚，既而悔焉，曰：「要當借汝頭以明法。

translations.literal: He also forbade his household slaves to go outside; then suddenly sent a slave to fetch broth from the public kitchen, and afterward regretted it, saying: 'I must borrow your head to make the law clear.'
translations.idiomatic: He had forbidden his household slaves to leave the premises, then impulsively sent one to the official kitchen for broth. Regretting the breach of his own rule, he said, 'I will have to take your head to uphold the law.'

sentences.zh: 」命斬奴，奴稱冤，監刑者疑不時決，軌並斬之。

translations.literal: He ordered the slave executed; the slave cried injustice; the overseer of the execution hesitated and did not carry it out promptly, so Gui executed them both.
translations.idiomatic: The slave was beheaded after pleading his innocence; when the executioner delayed, Gui killed him too.

sentences.zh: 後入朝，賜坐禦樓，容不肅，又坐對詔，帝怒曰：「公入蜀，車騎、驃騎從者二十人，公斬誅略盡，我隴種車騎，尚不足給公。

translations.literal: Later, entering court, he was granted a seat in the Imperial Tower but showed no proper decorum; again, seated while answering the edict, the emperor grew angry and said: 'When you went to Shu, twenty cavalrymen of the Palace Guard and Flying Cavalry followed you, and you executed nearly all of them; my Longzhong cavalry are not enough to supply you.'
translations.idiomatic: On a later visit to court he was invited to sit in the Imperial Tower but carried himself without due respect; when he answered an edict while still seated, the emperor exploded: 'You went to Shu with twenty of my palace horsemen and cut down almost every one of them. Even all the cavalry of Longzhong would not be enough for you.'

sentences.zh: 」因系詔獄。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was imprisoned in the edict prison.
translations.idiomatic: He was thrown into the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 俄釋之，還鎮益州。

translations.literal: Before long he was released and returned to govern Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was freed and sent back to his post at Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 軌與行台尚書韋雲起、郭行方素不協，及隱太子誅，詔至，軌內詔懷中，雲起問詔安在，軌不肯示，因執殺之。

translations.literal: Gui had long been at odds with Circuit Secretariat Directors Wei Yunqi and Guo Xingfang; when the Hidden Crown Prince was executed and the edict arrived, Gui hid it in his bosom; Yunqi asked where the edict was, and Gui refused to show it, then seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Gui had never gotten on with the circuit secretaries Wei Yunqi and Guo Xingfang. When the edict announcing the Hidden Crown Prince's death arrived, Gui tucked it inside his robe. Yunqi demanded to see it; Gui refused, then had him seized and killed.

sentences.zh: 行方懼，奔京師，得免。

translations.literal: Xingfang, in fear, fled to the capital and escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Xingfang fled to the capital and survived.

sentences.zh: 是歲，行台廢，授益州都督，加食邑戶六百。

translations.literal: That year the circuit headquarters was abolished; he was appointed Military Governor of Yizhou and granted six hundred additional households in his fief.
translations.idiomatic: That year the circuit office was dissolved. Gui became governor of Yizhou and received six hundred added fief households.

sentences.zh: 侄 琮

translations.literal: Nephew: Cong
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Cong

sentences.zh: 軌弟琮，有武幹。

translations.literal: Gui's younger brother Cong had military talent.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's younger brother Cong was a capable soldier.

sentences.zh: 大業末，犯法亡命太原，依高祖。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye era, having broken the law he fled as an outlaw to Taiyuan and attached himself to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Sui, he broke the law and fled to Taiyuan, where he entered Gaozu's service.

sentences.zh: 與秦王有憾，不自安。

translations.literal: He had a grievance against the Prince of Qin and did not feel secure.
translations.idiomatic: He had old bad blood with the Prince of Qin and lived in uneasy fear.

sentences.zh: 王方收天下豪英，降禮接之，與出入臥內，琮意乃釋。

translations.literal: The prince was then gathering heroes from throughout the realm, receiving them with lowered courtesy; he had Cong enter and leave his private quarters, and Cong's apprehensions were then relieved.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was recruiting the best men in the land and treating them with marked honor; he admitted Cong to his inner rooms day and night, and Cong's fears finally eased.

sentences.zh: 大將軍府建，引為統軍。

translations.literal: When the Grand General's Headquarters was established, Cong was recruited as a troop commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the grand general's headquarters was set up, Cong was made a division commander.

sentences.zh: 從平西河，破霍邑。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Xihe and captured Huoyi.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the pacification of Xihe and the capture of Huoyi.

sentences.zh: 授金紫光祿大夫，封扶風郡公。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Ribbon and enfeoffed as Duke of Fufeng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a grand master of splendid happiness with golden seal and ribbon and created Duke of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 從劉文靜擊屈突通於潼關，敗其將桑顯和，通遁去，琮以輕騎追獲于稠桑。

translations.literal: Following Liu Wenjing to attack Qu Tuotong at Tong Pass, he defeated Qu's general Sang Xianhe; Qu fled, and Cong with light cavalry pursued and captured him at Chousang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Wenjing he attacked Qu Tuotong at Tong Pass, routed Qu's general Sang Xianhe, and then ran Qu down with light cavalry at Chousang.

sentences.zh: 進兵下陝縣，拔太原倉。

translations.literal: He advanced and took Shan County and captured the Taiyuan granary.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed forward, seized Shan County, and took the Taiyuan granary.

sentences.zh: 遷左領軍大將軍，賜物五百段。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Left Vanguard Guards and granted five hundred rolls of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general of the left vanguard guards and rewarded with five hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 隋河陽都尉獨孤武潛謀歸款，命琮總萬騎，自柏崖迎之，逗留不進，武見殺，坐除名。

translations.literal: Sui Hedong Commandant Dugu Wu secretly plotted to surrender; Cong was ordered to command ten thousand cavalry to welcome him from Baiya, but delayed and did not advance; Wu was killed, and Cong was stripped of rank for the offense.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui commandant of Heyang, Dugu Wu, secretly offered to defect, Cong was told to take ten thousand horsemen and meet him at Baiya. He lingered and never moved; Wu was killed, and Cong was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 武德初，為右屯衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Early in the Wude era, he served as Grand General of the Right Garrison Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Wude reign he became grand general of the right garrison guard.

sentences.zh: 時將圖洛陽，詔琮留守陝，護饟道。

translations.literal: When they were about to target Luoyang, an edict ordered Cong to remain at Shan and protect the supply route.
translations.idiomatic: As the army prepared to move on Luoyang, Cong was ordered to hold Shan and keep the supply lines open.

sentences.zh: 王世充將羅士信數以兵鈔絕，琮使人說降之。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong's general Luo Shixin repeatedly cut off supplies with troops; Cong sent someone to persuade him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong's general Luo Shixin kept raiding the supply convoys, so Cong sent envoys to win him over.

sentences.zh: 東都平，檢校晉州總管。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Capital was pacified, he was made Acting General-in-Chief of Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Luoyang fell, he was made acting military governor of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 從隱太子平劉黑闥，以功封譙國公，賜黃金五十斤。

translations.literal: Following the Hidden Crown Prince to pacify Liu Heita, for his merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qiao State and granted fifty jin of gold.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Hidden Crown Prince against Liu Heita and, for his service, was created Duke of Qiao with fifty jin of gold.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈左衛大將軍，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously awarded Grand General of the Left Guard; posthumous title Respectful.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made grand general of the left guard, with the posthumous name Jing, "Respectful."

sentences.zh: 永徽五年，加贈特進。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yonghui, he was additionally posthumously honored as Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yonghui his honors were raised to special advancement.

sentences.zh: 侄 抗

translations.literal: Nephew: Kang
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Kang

sentences.zh: 威從兄子抗，字道生。

translations.literal: Wei's elder cousin's son Kang, courtesy name Daosheng.
translations.idiomatic: Kang, son of Wei's elder cousin, styled Daosheng.

sentences.zh: 父榮定，為隋洺州總管、陳國公，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: His father Rongding served as Sui General-in-Chief of Ming Prefecture and Duke of Chen State; posthumous title Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rongding had been Sui governor of Mingzhou and Duke of Chen, posthumously titled Yi.

sentences.zh: 母，隋文帝姊安成公主也。

translations.literal: His mother was Emperor Wen of Sui's elder sister, Princess Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Princess Ancheng, elder sister to Emperor Wen of Sui.

sentences.zh: 抗美容儀，性通率，涉見圖史。

translations.literal: Kang had handsome appearance, a frank and straightforward nature, and was versed in maps and historical texts.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome and open by nature, he was well read in history and the arts of statecraft.

sentences.zh: 以帝甥蚤貴，入太學，釋褐千牛備身、儀同三司。

translations.literal: As the emperor's nephew he rose early to eminence; he entered the Imperial Academy; upon first appointment he became Thousand-Ox Bodyguard and Yitong of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Being the emperor's nephew, he rose young: he studied at the Imperial Academy and on entering service became a thousand-ox guardsman with the rank of yitong, third rank.

sentences.zh: 侍父疾，束帶五旬不弛；

translations.literal: While attending his father's illness, he kept his girdle tied for fifty days without loosening it;
translations.idiomatic: While nursing his father he wore his official belt day and night for fifty days without once loosening it;

sentences.zh: 居喪，哀臒過常。

translations.literal: In mourning, his grief and emaciation exceeded the usual.
translations.idiomatic: in mourning he grieved so deeply that he wasted away beyond what custom allowed.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，累轉梁州刺史。

translations.literal: He inherited the title and successively served as Governor of Liang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded to his father's rank and eventually became governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 將之官，文帝幸其第，酣宴如家人禮。

translations.literal: When he was about to take up his post, Emperor Wen visited his residence and feasted merrily with him as with family.
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared to leave for his appointment, Emperor Wen came to his house and drank with him as one would with kin.

sentences.zh: 母卒，數號絕。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he repeatedly cried until he lost consciousness.
translations.idiomatic: At his mother's death he wept until he fainted again and again.

sentences.zh: 詔宮人節哭。

translations.literal: An edict ordered palace attendants to restrain his mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent palace attendants to urge him to moderate his grief.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，為岐州刺史，轉幽州總管，所至以寬惠聞。

translations.literal: After slightly more than a year, he became Governor of Qi Prefecture, then transferred to General-in-Chief of You Prefecture; wherever he went he was known for leniency and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he was made governor of Qizhou, then military governor of Youzhou; everywhere he served he was praised for mercy and generosity.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒反，煬帝疑抗為應，遣李子雄馳往代之。

translations.literal: When Prince Han Liang rebelled, Emperor Yang suspected Kang of colluding with him and dispatched Li Zixiong posthaste to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Han Liang rose in revolt, Emperor Yang suspected Kang of siding with him and sent Li Zixiong at full speed to relieve him of command.

sentences.zh: 子雄因誣抗得諒書不奏，按鞫無狀，然坐是遂廢。

translations.literal: Zixiong falsely accused Kang of receiving a letter from Liang without reporting it; investigation found no evidence, yet Kang was nonetheless dismissed for this matter.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zixiong claimed Kang had received a letter from Liang and concealed it. The inquiry turned up nothing, but Kang was ruined all the same.

sentences.zh: 抗與高祖少相狎，及楊玄感反，抗謂高祖曰：「玄感為我先耳，李氏名在圖錄，天所啟也。

translations.literal: Kang and Gaozu had been close since youth; when Yang Xuangan rebelled, Kang told Gaozu: 'Xuangan has acted before us, but the Li surname is recorded in the prophetic texts—it is heaven's opening.'
translations.idiomatic: Kang had known Gaozu since they were young. When Yang Xuangan rebelled, he told Gaozu, "Xuangan has merely gone first. The house of Li is named in the books of fate—Heaven itself has opened the way."

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「為禍始不祥，公無妄言。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: 'Speaking of calamity at the outset is inauspicious; do not speak rashly, sir.'
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu replied, "It is ill luck to talk of disaster before it comes. Say no more, sir."

sentences.zh: 」煬帝遣抗出靈武，逴護長城，聞高祖已定京師，喜曰：「此吾家婿，豁達有大度，真撥亂主也。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang dispatched Kang to Lingwu to patrol and guard the Great Wall from afar; hearing that Gaozu had secured the capital, Kang rejoiced and said: 'This son-in-law of our house is open-hearted and magnanimous—a true ruler who can quell turmoil.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang sent Kang to Lingwu to guard the distant reaches of the Great Wall. When word came that Gaozu had taken the capital, Kang exulted: "That son-in-law of ours is broad-minded and bold—the very man to set the realm right."

sentences.zh: 」因歸長安。

translations.literal: Thereupon he returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He went back to Chang'an at once.

sentences.zh: 高祖見之喜，握手曰：「李氏果王，何如？

translations.literal: Gaozu was delighted to see him, took his hand and said: 'The Li surname has indeed become sovereign—how about that?'
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu greeted him with joy, clasped his hand, and said, "So the house of Li truly holds the throne—what do you think of that?"

sentences.zh: 」因置酒為樂，授將作大匠兼納言，尋罷為左武候大將軍。

translations.literal: He then set out wine for merriment, appointed him Director of Palace Construction and concurrently Censor, and soon removed him to Grand General of the Left Military Guard.
translations.idiomatic: They drank in celebration. Kang was made director of palace construction and also censor, then shortly afterward grand general of the left military guard.

sentences.zh: 帝聽朝，或引升禦坐，既退，入臥內，從容談笑，極平生歡，以兄呼之，宮中稱為舅，或留宿禁省，侍燕豫，然未嘗幹朝廷事。

translations.literal: When the emperor held court, he sometimes had Kang ascend to the imperial seat; after retiring, he entered the private quarters and talked and laughed at ease, sharing the fullest friendship of a lifetime; he addressed Kang as elder brother, and within the palace Kang was called Uncle; sometimes he was kept overnight in the forbidden offices to attend banquets, yet he never meddled in court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At audience Gaozu would sometimes seat him beside the throne; afterward they withdrew to the inner rooms to talk as old friends. The emperor called him "elder brother," and the palace knew him as "Uncle." He often stayed the night inside the palace for feasts, but never once interfered in government.

sentences.zh: 後從秦王平薛舉，功第一；

translations.literal: Later he followed the Prince of Qin to pacify Xue Ju, ranking first in merit;
translations.idiomatic: He later followed the Prince of Qin against Xue Ju and stood first in merit;

sentences.zh: 又從征王世充。

translations.literal: he also followed the campaign against Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: and took part in the campaign against Wang Shichong as well.

sentences.zh: 東都平，冊勳於廟者九人，抗與從弟軌與焉。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Capital was pacified, nine men had their merit recorded in the ancestral temple; Kang and his cousin Gui were among them.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell, only nine men were honored with temple inscriptions for their deeds; Kang and his cousin Gui were two of them.

sentences.zh: 賜女樂一部，珍幣不貲。

translations.literal: He was granted a troupe of female musicians and treasures beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: He received a full company of court musicians and riches beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司徒，諡曰密。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously awarded Minister over the Masses; posthumous title Mi.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made minister over the masses, with the posthumous name Mi, "Prudent."

sentences.zh: 子衍、靜、誕，衍襲爵。

translations.literal: His sons were Yan, Jing, and Dan; Yan inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: He left three sons—Yan, Jing, and Dan—and Yan succeeded to the rank.

sentences.zh: 侄孫 靜

translations.literal: Grand-nephew: Jing
translations.idiomatic: Grand-nephew: Jing

sentences.zh: 靜字元休，在隋佐親衛，以父得罪煬帝，久不之進。

translations.literal: Jing, courtesy name Yuanxiu, served in the Personal Guard during the Sui; because his father had offended Emperor Yang, he long went unpromoted.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, styled Yuanxiu, had served in the Sui emperor's personal guard, but after his father fell from Yang's favor he languished without advancement for years.

sentences.zh: 高祖入京師，擢并州大總管府長史。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered the capital, Jing was promoted to Chief Administrator of the Taiyuan Grand General's Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the capital, Jing was made chief administrator of the Taiyuan headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時突厥數為邊患，糧道不屬，靜表請屯田太原，以省饋運。

translations.literal: At that time the Turks repeatedly troubled the border and supply routes were cut; Jing memorialized requesting agricultural colonies at Taiyuan to reduce transport of provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks were raiding the frontier and supply lines were failing, so Jing proposed garrison farming around Taiyuan to ease the burden of long-distance grain transport.

sentences.zh: 議者以流亡未復，不宜重困，於是召入與裴寂、蕭瑀、封倫廷議，寂等不能屈，帝從之，歲收粟十萬斛。

translations.literal: Critics said refugees had not yet returned and it was inappropriate to burden them heavily; therefore he was summoned for court deliberation with Pei Ji, Xiao Yu, and Feng Lun; Ji and the others could not refute him; the emperor followed his advice; annually they harvested one hundred thousand bushels of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Opponents argued that the displaced had not yet resettled and the region should not be taxed further, so Jing was called in to debate Pei Ji, Xiao Yu, and Feng Lun before the throne. None could overturn his case; the emperor agreed, and the fields soon yielded a hundred thousand bushels a year.

sentences.zh: 詔檢校并州大總管。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Acting Grand General of Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made acting grand general of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 又請斷石嶺以為鄣塞，制突厥之入。

translations.literal: He also requested blocking Shiling to serve as a barrier fort, controlling Turkic incursions.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that Shiling be fortified as a barrier against Turk raids.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，授司農卿，封信都縣男。

translations.literal: When Taizong acceded, he was appointed Minister of Agriculture and enfeoffed as Baron of Xindu County.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong came to the throne, Jing became minister of agriculture and was created baron of Xindu.

sentences.zh: 趙元楷為少卿，靜鄙其聚斂，因會官屬大言曰：「如煬帝奢侈，竭四海自奉，司農須公矣。

translations.literal: Zhao Yuankai served as Vice Minister; Jing despised his exactions; at a gathering of officials he declared loudly: 'If Emperor Yang were extravagant, draining the four seas to serve himself, the Ministry of Agriculture would need you, sir.'
translations.idiomatic: His deputy Zhao Yuankai was a notorious extortionist. At a meeting of the ministry Jing said openly, "Under Emperor Yang, who drained the empire to feed his luxuries, the Ministry of Agriculture would have needed a man like you."

sentences.zh: 今天子躬節儉，屈一人安兆庶，惡用公哉？

translations.literal: 'But today's Son of Heaven personally practices thrift, restraining one man to comfort the myriad people—of what use are you?'
translations.idiomatic: "But this emperor lives plainly and burdens one official so that the people may rest—what use has he for you?"

sentences.zh: 」元楷大慚。

translations.literal: Yuankai was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankai flushed with shame.

sentences.zh: 改夏州都督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Military Commissioner of Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was reassigned as military commissioner of Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 突厥攜貳，諸將出征者過靜，靜為陳虜中虛實，諸將由是大克獲。

translations.literal: When the Turks showed divided allegiance, generals on campaign passed by Jing; Jing explained the enemy's strengths and weaknesses, and the generals thereby achieved great victories and captures.
translations.idiomatic: As the Turks began to split among themselves, commanders marching north stopped to consult Jing about enemy conditions; thanks to his intelligence they won one great victory after another.

sentences.zh: 又間其部落，郁射所部鬱孤尼等九俟斤皆內附。

translations.literal: He also sowed discord among their tribes; nine irkins including Yeguni of Yushe's division all submitted inward.
translations.idiomatic: He also set tribe against tribe until nine tribal chiefs, including Yeguni under Yushe, came over to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，賜馬百匹、羊千口。

translations.literal: The emperor commended him and granted a hundred horses and a thousand sheep.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him and rewarded him with a hundred horses and a thousand sheep.

sentences.zh: 及禽頡利，詔處其眾河南。

translations.literal: When Jiali was captured, an edict ordered settling his people south of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiali Khan was taken, the court ordered his people resettled south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 靜上書曰：「夷狄窮則搏噬，飽則群聚，不可以刑法繩、仁義教也。

translations.literal: Jing submitted a memorial saying: 'When barbarians are desperate they bite; when sated they gather in herds—they cannot be bound by penal law or taught by benevolence and righteousness.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing wrote in protest: "Barbarians fight when cornered and herd together when fed. Neither punishment nor moral teaching will hold them."

sentences.zh: 衣食仰給，不恃耕桑。

translations.literal: 'Their food and clothing depend on others; they do not rely on farming and sericulture.'
translations.idiomatic: "They live on what others provide and know nothing of tillage or silk."

sentences.zh: 今損有為之民，資無知之虜，得之無益於治，失之不害於化。

translations.literal: 'Now to harm productive subjects in order to support ignorant barbarians gains nothing for good order and loses nothing for civilization if they are lost.'
translations.idiomatic: "To burden our own working people to feed these unknowing tribes helps no cause of order, and their loss would not harm our civilization."

sentences.zh: 況首丘未忘，則一旦變生，犯我王略矣。

translations.literal: 'Moreover, if longing for home is not forgotten, then one morning change will arise and they will violate our royal domain.'
translations.idiomatic: "And if they still remember their old homes, rebellion may come in a single morning and they will strike at the heart of the realm."

sentences.zh: 不如因其破亡，假以賢王一號，妻之宗女，披其土地部落，使權弱勢分，易為羈制，則世為籓臣矣。

translations.literal: 'Better, while they are broken and ruined, to grant one of them the title of a worthy king, marry him to a princess of the imperial clan, divide their lands and tribes so that power is weak and strength scattered, making them easy to control by reins—then for generations they will be vassal ministers.'
translations.idiomatic: "Better to use their defeat: invest one leader as a client king, marry him to an imperial clanswoman, and break up their lands and tribes until they are weak and divided. Then they can be led on a leash and remain vassals for generations."

sentences.zh: 」帝雖不從，然嘉其忠，優詔答曰：「北方之務，悉以相委，以卿為甯朔大使，朕無北顧憂矣。

translations.literal: The emperor though he did not follow the advice, yet commended his loyalty, and replied with a gracious edict: 'Northern affairs I entirely entrust to you; with you as Ambassador Pacifying the North, I have no worry looking north.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected the plan but honored his loyalty with a warm reply: "All northern affairs are yours. With you as ambassador pacifying the north, I need not look over my shoulder."

sentences.zh: 」再遷民部尚書。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Minister of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made minister of the household.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰肅。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Su.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Su, "Solemn."

sentences.zh: 子逵，尚遂安公主，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Kui married Princess Sui'an and inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kui married Princess Sui'an and succeeded to the rank.

sentences.zh: 侄孫 誕

translations.literal: Grand-nephew: Dan
translations.idiomatic: Grand-nephew: Dan

sentences.zh: 誕，隋末起家朝請郎。

translations.literal: Dan, at the end of the Sui, began his career as Court Gentleman for Consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Dan entered service at the end of the Sui as a court gentleman for consultation.

sentences.zh: 義甯初，辟丞相府祭酒，封安豐郡公，尚襄陽公主。

translations.literal: Early in Yining, he was recruited as Libationer of the Chancellor's Office, enfeoffed as Duke of Anfeng Commandery, and married Princess Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yining era he became libationer in the chancellor's office, was created Duke of Anfeng, and married Princess Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 從秦王征薛舉，為元帥府司馬。

translations.literal: He followed the Prince of Qin in the campaign against Xue Ju, serving as Chief of Staff of the Marshal's Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with the Prince of Qin against Xue Ju as chief of staff of the marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 累遷太常卿。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in time to minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 高祖諸子幼，未出宮者十余王，國司家事，皆誕主之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu's sons were still young, more than ten princes who had not yet left the palace—all household affairs of their principalities were managed by Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's sons were still young, and more than ten princes who had not yet left the palace relied on Dan to run the domestic affairs of their fiefs.

sentences.zh: 出為梁州都督。

translations.literal: He went out as Military Commissioner of Liang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as military commissioner of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，召授右領軍大將軍，進莘國公，為宗正卿。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenguan he was summoned and appointed Grand General of the Right Vanguard Guards, advanced to Duke of Xin State, and made Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he was recalled as grand general of the right vanguard guards, created Duke of Xin, and made director of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 太宗與語，昏謬失對。

translations.literal: Taizong conversed with him; muddled and confused, he gave wrong replies.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong spoke with him, but he answered in a confused, incoherent way.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔曰：「誕比衰耗，不能事，朕知而任之，是謂不明。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict said: 'Dan has lately declined and cannot serve; I knew this yet appointed him—that is called not being clear-sighted.'
translations.idiomatic: An edict then said, "Dan has grown feeble and can no longer serve. I knew it and still used him—that is poor judgment."

sentences.zh: 且為官擇人者治，為人擇官者亂。

translations.literal: 'Moreover, choosing men for offices is governing; choosing offices for men is disorder.'
translations.idiomatic: "To choose the right man for an office is government; to choose an office for a man is chaos."

sentences.zh: 其以光祿大夫罷就第。

translations.literal: 'Let him retire to his residence with the rank of Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.'
translations.idiomatic: "Let him retire home with the rank of grand master for splendid happiness."

sentences.zh: 」卒，贈工部尚書、荊州刺史，諡曰安。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously given Minister of Works and Governor of Jing Prefecture; posthumous title An.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made minister of works and governor of Jingzhou, with the posthumous name An, "Peaceful."

sentences.zh: 侄 璡

translations.literal: Nephew: Jin
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Jin

sentences.zh: 抗弟璡，字之推，性沈厚。

translations.literal: Kang's younger brother Jin, courtesy name Zhitui, was deep and steady in nature.
translations.idiomatic: Kang's younger brother Jin, styled Zhitui, was grave and steady by nature.

sentences.zh: 隋大業末，為扶風太守。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye era in Sui, he was governor of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui he was governor of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 唐兵起，以郡歸，曆民部尚書。

translations.literal: When Tang forces rose, he surrendered the commandery and successively served as Minister of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang rose he surrendered his commandery and later became minister of the household.

sentences.zh: 從秦王平薛仁杲，賜錦袍。

translations.literal: He followed the Prince of Qin to pacify Xue Rengao and was granted a brocade robe.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Prince of Qin against Xue Rengao and received a brocade robe as reward.

sentences.zh: 尋鎮益州，時蜀盜賊多，皆討平之。

translations.literal: Soon he governed Yizhou; at the time bandits and robbers were numerous in Shu, and he pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posted to Yizhou, where he put down the many bandits of Shu.

sentences.zh: 與皇甫無逸不協，數相訴毀，因請入朝，至半道，詔還之。

translations.literal: He did not get along with Huangfu Wuyi and repeatedly accused each other; he requested to enter court, and halfway there an edict ordered him back.
translations.idiomatic: He feuded with Huangfu Wuyi and they repeatedly denounced each other. He asked to return to court, but halfway there an edict sent him back.

sentences.zh: 璡內憂恐。

translations.literal: Jin was inwardly fearful and anxious.
translations.idiomatic: Jin lived in inward dread.

sentences.zh: 會使者至，璡引宴臥內，厚餉遺。

translations.literal: When an envoy arrived, Jin entertained him in his private quarters and gave lavish gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When an envoy came, Jin entertained him in his private rooms and gave rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 無逸以聞，坐免官。

translations.literal: Wuyi reported this and Jin was dismissed from office for the offense.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi reported the matter and Jin was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授秘書監，封鄧國公。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Duke of Deng State.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made director of the secretariat and created Duke of Deng.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，遷將作大匠，詔脩洛陽宮，鑿池起山，務極侈浮，費不勝算。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenguan, transferred to Director of Palace Construction; ordered to repair Luoyang Palace, dig ponds and raise hills, striving for extreme luxury, with expenses beyond calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he became director of palace construction and was ordered to rebuild Luoyang Palace with ponds and artificial hills in reckless extravagance at ruinous cost.

sentences.zh: 太宗怒，詔毀之，免其官。

translations.literal: Taizong grew angry, ordered it destroyed, and removed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was furious, ordered the work torn down, and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 以酆王納璡女為妃，復位。

translations.literal: Because the Prince of Feng took Jin's daughter as consort, his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Feng married Jin's daughter, his post was restored.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈禮部尚書，諡曰安。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously given Minister of Rites; posthumous title An.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made minister of rites, with the posthumous name An.

sentences.zh: 璡有巧思，工書。

translations.literal: Jin had ingenious ideas and was skilled in calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was ingenious and a fine calligrapher.

sentences.zh: 武德中，與太常少卿祖孝孫受詔定雅樂，是正鐘律雲。

translations.literal: In Wude, together with Vice Minister of Ceremonies Zu Xiaosun he received an edict to fix court music and correct bell pitch.
translations.idiomatic: During Wude he and Vice Minister Zu Xiaosun were ordered to set the court music and correct the pitch of the bells.

sentences.zh: 從孫 德玄

translations.literal: Great-grandnephew: Dexuan
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandnephew: Dexuan

sentences.zh: 威從孫德玄，隋大業中，起家國學生。

translations.literal: Wei's great-grandnephew Dexuan, in the Daye era of Sui, began his career as a student of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Dexuan, Wei's great-grandnephew, entered the Imperial Academy at the end of the Sui.

sentences.zh: 祖照，尚周文帝義陽公主，封钜鹿郡公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhao married Princess Yiyang of Emperor Wen of Zhou and was enfeoffed as Duke of Julu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhao married Princess Yiyang, daughter of Emperor Wen of Zhou, and was created Duke of Julu.

sentences.zh: 父彥，襲爵，終隋西平太守。

translations.literal: His father Yan inherited the title and ended as Sui governor of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan succeeded to the title and ended his career as Sui governor of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 兄德明，師事陳留王孝逸，通知文史。

translations.literal: His elder brother Deming studied under Wang Xiaoyi of Chenliu and was versed in literature and history.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Deming studied under Wang Xiaoyi of Chenliu and was learned in letters and history.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒反，遣將綦良攻黎州。

translations.literal: When Prince Han Liang rebelled, he sent general Qi Liang to attack Li Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Han Liang rebelled, he sent General Qi Liang against Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 德明年十八，募士五千，號令嚴整，倍道擊賊，破之。

translations.literal: Deming at eighteen recruited five thousand men; his commands were strict and orderly; marching at double speed he attacked the rebels and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Deming, only eighteen, raised five thousand men, kept them under iron discipline, forced a rapid march, and routed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 以功擢累齊王府屬。

translations.literal: For merit he was repeatedly promoted among staff of the Prince of Qi's palace.
translations.idiomatic: For this feat he rose through the staff of the Prince of Qi's household.

sentences.zh: 坐事免。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was later dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 高祖兵叩長安，而宗室孝基、神符、道宗及竇誕、趙慈景等並系獄，隋將衛文升、陰世師欲殺之，德明諫曰：「罪不在此，殺之無傷於彼，祗取怨焉，不如縱之。
