translations.literal: When Gaozu's army knocked at Chang'an, clansmen Xiaoji, Shenfu, Daozong, Dou Dan, Zhao Cijing, and others were all imprisoned; Sui generals Wei Wensheng and Yin Shishi wished to kill them; Deming remonstrated: 'The crime is not with these men; killing them does no harm to the enemy—it only wins resentment. Better to release them.'
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu's army reached Chang'an, Xiaoji, Shenfu, Daozong, Dou Dan, Zhao Cijing, and other kinsmen were in prison. The Sui generals Wei Wensheng and Yin Shishi meant to execute them. Deming urged, "These men are not guilty. Killing them will not hurt the enemy, only breed hatred. Release them."

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: They thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: They held their hand.

sentences.zh: 長安平，謁高祖，終不自言，時稱長者。

translations.literal: When Chang'an was pacified, he paid respects to Gaozu and to the end never spoke of it himself; the age called him a man of length.
translations.idiomatic: After Chang'an fell he presented himself to Gaozu but never mentioned what he had done, and contemporaries called him a true elder.

sentences.zh: 拜考功郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Bureau of Merit.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed director of the bureau of merit.

sentences.zh: 從秦王擊王世充。

translations.literal: He followed the Prince of Qin to attack Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Prince of Qin against Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 封顯武男，曆常、愛二州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Xianwu; successively governed Chang and Ai prefectures; died.
translations.idiomatic: He was created baron of Xianwu, served as governor of Chang and Ai, and died.

sentences.zh: 德玄始為高祖丞相府千牛，曆太宗時不甚顯，高宗以舊臣，自殿中少監為御史大夫，歲中遷司元太常伯。

translations.literal: Dexuan began as Thousand-Ox of Gaozu's chancellor's office; through Taizong's reign he was not very prominent; Gaozong, honoring him as an old minister, promoted him from Vice Supervisor of the Palace to Censor-in-Chief, and within the year to Grand Master of Harmonious Origin and Director of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Dexuan began as a thousand-ox guardsman in Gaozu's chancellor's office and was little noticed under Taizong. Gaozong, treating him as an old servant, raised him from vice supervisor of the palace to censor-in-chief and within a year to grand master of harmonious origin and director of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 時帝又以源直心為奉常正卿，劉祥道為司刑太常伯，上官儀為西台侍極，郝處俊為太子左中護，凡十餘人，皆帝自擇，以示宰相李勣等，皆頓首謝。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor also had Yuan Zhiyuan as Director of Harmonious Rites, Liu Xiangdao as Grand Master of Punitive Rites, Shangguan Yi as Attendant of the Western Terrace, Hao Chujun as Left Protector of the Heir—more than ten men in all, all chosen by the emperor himself; he showed them to Chancellor Li Ji and the others, and all bowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at the same time named Yuan Zhiyuan director of harmonious rites, Liu Xiangdao grand master of punitive rites, Shangguan Yi attendant of the western terrace, Hao Chujun left protector of the heir, and more than ten others—all his own choices, shown to Li Ji and the other chancellors, who bowed in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 麟德初，進檢校左相，勤職約己，天子嘗臨朝，咨其清素，加以賜賚。

translations.literal: Early in Linde, he was advanced to Acting Left Chancellor; diligent in office and restrained in personal conduct; the Son of Heaven sometimes at audience inquired about his frugality and granted him rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Linde he became acting left chancellor, careful in duty and spare in living. The emperor sometimes asked after his frugality at court and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 居位數年，贊圖封禪事，與李勣皆為使。

translations.literal: After several years in office, he assisted in the feng and shan rites; with Li Ji he both served as envoy.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he helped plan the feng and shan sacrifices and served as envoy together with Li Ji.

sentences.zh: 帝次濮陽，問古謂帝丘，德玄不能對，許敬宗具道其然，帝稱善。

translations.literal: When the emperor halted at Puyang, he asked what antiquity called Emperor's Mound; Dexuan could not answer; Xu Jingzong fully explained it, and the emperor praised this.
translations.idiomatic: At Puyang the emperor asked what antiquity called the Mound of the Emperor. Dexuan could not say; Xu Jingzong answered fully, and the emperor praised him.

sentences.zh: 敬宗自矜於人，德玄知，不為忤，眾服其量。

translations.literal: Jingzong was self-conceited toward others; Dexuan knew it yet did not take offense; all admired his magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong was vain toward others, but Dexuan knew it and never quarreled; everyone respected his forbearance.

sentences.zh: 禮成，進爵二級。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed, he was advanced two ranks in nobility.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished his noble rank was raised two steps.

sentences.zh: 以弟德遠未及爵，願分封，詔可，故德玄封钜鹿男，德遠樂安男。

translations.literal: Because his younger brother Deyuan had not yet received a noble title, he requested the fief be divided; the edict approved it; therefore Dexuan was enfeoffed Baron of Julu and Deyuan Baron of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Deyuan had no title yet, so he asked that the fief be split. The emperor agreed: Dexuan became baron of Julu and Deyuan baron of Le'an.

sentences.zh: 德玄迎時取合，未嘗有過，然無它補益。

translations.literal: Dexuan accommodated the times and pleased his superiors, never having faults, yet made no other contributions.
translations.idiomatic: Dexuan kept to the mood of the court and pleased his superiors without fault, yet added nothing of substance.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十九，贈光祿大夫，幽州都督，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-nine; posthumously given Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Military Governor of You Prefecture; posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-nine and was posthumously made grand master for splendid happiness and military governor of Youzhou, with the posthumous name Gong, "Respectful."

sentences.zh: 贊曰：高、竇雖緣外戚姻家，然自以才猷結天子，廁跡名臣，垂榮無窮，時有遇合，故見諸事業。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Gao and Dou, though linked by marriage as affinal kin, yet by their own talent won the Son of Heaven, shared place among famed ministers, and glory without end—at times fortune met them, hence they appear in deeds.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: The Gao and Dou lines, though they rose through marriage ties, won the throne by talent, stood among great ministers, and enjoyed lasting honor. Fortune met them at the right moment, and so their deeds are recorded here.

sentences.zh: 古來賢豪，不遭與運，埋光鏟采，與草木俱腐者，可勝吒哉！

translations.literal: Since antiquity able and heroic men who did not meet with the age, buried light and buried brilliance, rotting with grass and trees—who can count them! How deeply to be lamented!
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity, how many able men never found their time, hid their light, and rotted away with the grass—beyond numbering. It is cause for deep sighing.

sentences.zh: 竇宗自魏訖唐，支胄扶疏數百年，所馮厚矣。

translations.literal: The Dou clan from Wei to Tang, branches luxuriant for several hundred years, leaned on thick support.
translations.idiomatic: The Dou house flourished from Wei through Tang for centuries on powerful patronage.
